name: Photosynthesis
what: Covers the purpose of photosynthesis, the structure of the chloroplast, and the inputs, outputs and locations of the light dependent and light independent stages in C3 plants. Includes the roles of key molecules such as Rubisco, ATP synthase, NADP+ and RuBP.
why: Photosynthesis is the foundation of almost all food chains on Earth and is a core example of how biochemical pathways convert one form of energy to another. Understanding its stages and molecular components is essential for VCE Biology assessment and for making sense of how organisms regulate energy.

items.title: I can state the purpose of photosynthesis
items.what: Photosynthesis is an anabolic reaction in which light energy is used to convert carbon dioxide and water into glucose and oxygen inside the chloroplast.
items.why: Knowing the purpose distinguishes photosynthesis from cellular respiration and establishes why autotrophs can sustain themselves without consuming other organisms.
items.example: A spinach plant uses light energy, CO2 from the air and H2O from the soil to produce glucose for growth and O2 as a waste product.

items.title: I can explain the general function of the chloroplast
items.what: The chloroplast is the organelle in plant and algal cells where photosynthesis occurs. It contains chlorophyll in the thylakoid membranes and enzymes in the stroma that carry out the two stages of photosynthesis.
items.why: Linking organelle structure to function is a recurring assessment skill. Understanding why the chloroplast is the site of photosynthesis requires knowing what each internal region does.
items.example: Chlorophyll is embedded in the thylakoid membranes of the grana, so light energy is captured there during the light dependent stage.

items.title: I can draw and label a chloroplast and recall the function of its key structures
items.what: A chloroplast has an outer membrane, inner membrane, grana (stacks of thylakoid membranes), stroma, ribosomes, DNA and starch granules. Each structure has a specific role in photosynthesis.
items.why: Labelled diagrams are frequently assessed in VCE Biology. Knowing the function of each structure allows you to connect structure to the stages of photosynthesis.
items.example: The stroma surrounds the grana and is the site of the light independent stage (Calvin Cycle), so it contains many ribosomes to produce the enzymes needed for those reactions.

items.title: I can state the word equation and balanced chemical equation for photosynthesis
items.what: Word equation: carbon dioxide + water → oxygen + glucose (requires light energy and chlorophyll). Balanced equation: 6CO2 + 12H2O → 6O2 + 6H2O + C6H12O6, or simplified: 6CO2 + 6H2O → 6O2 + C6H12O6.
items.why: The equation summarises all inputs and outputs of photosynthesis. In assessments, the arrow must include 'light energy' and 'chlorophyll' to be awarded marks.
items.example: If a question asks for the equation for photosynthesis, writing 'carbon dioxide + water → oxygen + glucose' without 'light energy' and 'chlorophyll' on the arrow will not receive full marks.

items.title: I can summarise the inputs, outputs and location of the two stages of photosynthesis in C3 plants
items.what: The light dependent stage occurs on the thylakoid membranes and uses light energy and water to produce ATP, NADPH and O2. The light independent stage (Calvin Cycle) occurs in the stroma and uses CO2, ATP and NADPH to produce glucose and regenerate RuBP.
items.why: Tabulating inputs, outputs and locations is a direct Study Design requirement and a common exam question format. Confusing the two stages is a frequent student error.
items.example: In a table: Light dependent stage — inputs: light energy, H2O; outputs: ATP, NADPH, O2; location: thylakoid membranes.

items.title: I can outline what occurs during the light dependent and light independent stages of photosynthesis
items.what: In the light dependent stage, chlorophyll absorbs light energy, water is split by photolysis producing O2, H+ and electrons, ATP is synthesised by ATP synthase and NADP+ is reduced to NADPH. In the light independent stage, RuBP combines with CO2 (via Rubisco) to form PGA, which is converted to PGAL using ATP and NADPH, then PGAL forms glucose and regenerates RuBP.
items.why: Describing both stages in sequence shows understanding of how the two stages depend on each other, which is tested in extended response questions.
items.example: The ATP and NADPH produced in the light dependent stage are transported to the stroma and used to drive the reactions of the Calvin Cycle in the light independent stage.

items.title: I can describe the role of Rubisco and ATP synthase in photosynthesis
items.what: Rubisco (RuBP carboxylase) is the enzyme that catalyses the fixation of CO2 to RuBP in the Calvin Cycle, producing PGA. ATP synthase is an enzyme embedded in the thylakoid membrane that catalyses the synthesis of ATP from ADP and inorganic phosphate using energy from electron flow.
items.why: Both enzymes are named in the Study Design and are commonly used in exam questions to test understanding of specific molecular roles within a broader pathway.
items.example: If Rubisco is inhibited, CO2 cannot be fixed to RuBP and no PGA is produced, so the Calvin Cycle stops and glucose cannot be made.
